Pegasus · Triage Case design review · 5 October 2026

The photographs first. Everything else in reach.

Three ways to lay out a Triage Case around its vehicle images, all on the current Pegasus shell. All three share the changes you asked for: one Actions menu, the composer for chasers, Determinations in a dialog, a Correspondence tab under Files, and no Open message.

One Actions menu

Assign, Determinations, Complete Triage, Await information, Send chaser or Reply with outcome, Link or Unlink case, and Cancel Triage (red, last) now share one menu. The assignee stays visible in the ribbon. A mockup switch shows each state’s next step beside the menu (item B).

Correspondence like a Case

Files gains a Correspondence tab: the request e-mail, the chasers and the replies, each opened in the message dialog. Send chaser opens the Inbox composer as an overlay. The inline chaser form and Open message have been removed.

Determinations in a dialog

The settled finding reads as greyed boxes. You record or change it in the Determinations dialog, or with Record correction once the Triage is Completed.

A

Image stage

One large photograph with a filmstrip, directly under the ribbon.

The page keeps today’s single column. A large lead image with a filmstrip takes the top of the record. Below it come a two-box Determinations read-out, then Files (Documents and Correspondence), then Notes.

Why choose it
It is the closest to today’s page and the easiest to move to. One image at a time, at full width, is the best size for judging damage.
Tradeoff
Determinations and Notes are below the images, so you scroll down to see the record’s status beside a photograph.

B

Inspection split

Recommended

A persistent viewer on the left; the decision, notes and status on the right.

A two-column workspace. On the left is a large viewer with Tag and Crop in place and thumbnails underneath. On the right are stacked cards: Determinations, Correspondence status, Exact response evidence when present, and Notes. Files (Documents and Correspondence) run full width below.

Why choose it
The photographs and the decision stay side by side, so you can assess and record without scrolling or opening the viewer.
Tradeoff
It is the densest layout. Below 1180px it folds into one column, and its image is smaller than A’s at the same width.
Explore design B →Finding recordedSend chaser
C

Contact sheet

A sticky status bar, then tabs for Images, Files and Notes.

A sticky summary bar holds the state, the two determinations and the assignee. Below it, tabs switch between Images (the default, a large-thumbnail contact sheet grouped by tag), Files (Documents and Correspondence) and Notes.

Why choose it
It gives the most room to images, puts every photograph on screen at once and needs the least scrolling.
Tradeoff
Files and Notes are one click away rather than on the page. Tabs change the shape of the page compared with the regular Case record.
Explore design C →Finding recordedSend chaser
Recommended: B · Inspection split. The photographs and the decision stay side by side, which suits the task: look, decide, record. A is the smallest change from today. C gives images the most room but moves Files and Notes behind tabs.
Try it: open the Actions menu, record determinations, complete the Triage, send a chaser through the composer, open a message from the Correspondence tab, and tag or crop an image. Mockup controls cover all 13 states. Read the notes and the lettered sign-off items. These are offline design artifacts and do not establish how the application behaves.
